pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-03.png with Read and looked at it directly. It read without problems. The page has 4 panels: a top row with a left and a narrower right panel, then a wide middle panel and a wide bottom panel.
pages.observation: My reading order: (1) Top-left panel. 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' The tail points to Ravi, who is at upper right, with Meera at lower left. (2) Top-right panel. 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' The tail points to Meera, with Ravi at the left edge partly cut off by the frame. (3) Middle panel. 'Yes, please.' The tail points to Ravi, who is on the left, with Meera on the right. (4) Bottom panel. 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.' The tail points to Meera, who is on the right, with Ravi on the left. The dialogue chain is natural question and answer. Issues: (a) There is a left-right swap. In panel 1 Ravi is on the right and Meera on the left, but in panels 2 to 4 Ravi is on the left and Meera on the right. That breaks screen direction across the first panel transition. (b) Meera calls him 'Ravi' although he never gives his name on the page. The registration itself, between 'Yes, please' and 'all set', happens off-panel. That is acceptable, but the large middle panel could show the details being given. (c) Nothing signals the scene change from page 2's staff onboarding to a patient arriving at reception (time, place, or a new person). A short caption or establishing beat would help. (d) Ravi is not introduced as a patient other than by implication.
